newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Shell sees Nigerian oil output doubling by 2010.
newsitem.headline: Shell sees Nigerian oil output doubling by 2010.

text.p: Nigerian oil production could nearly double to four million barrels per day by the year 2010, a senior industry official said on Tuesday.

Basil Omiyi, Shell Petroleum Development Co, Nigeria general manager relations and environment, said at a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference that Nigeria would continue to play a major role in world oil supply.
"We see Nigerian production growing, doubling to four million barrels by 2010," Omiyi said.
Nigeria, the largest oil producer in Africa, currently produces around 2.15 million barrels per day (bpd) with reserves of 22 billion barrels.
Omiyi said the industry could produce about three million bpd by the end of 2002.
"There is significant opportunity for growth, for private investment especially in gas," he added.
He said Nigeria had abundant reserves of natural gas which it currently flares, although the government had committed itself to eliminating all gas flaring by 2010.
In addition, the country's Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) project was under construction and projects to pipe gas to neighbouring countries were being studied.
"There are dicussions ongoing for a pipeline to Benin, Togo and Ghana," he said.
The $4 billion LNG project is about 40 percent completed and is scheduled to come on stream in October 1999.
